triggers: a scalar-FMA Metal GEMM runs far below MMA-peak TFLOPS
an LLM-generated or hand-written Metal GEMM lacks simdgroup_matrix usage

payload.goal: Replace scalar FMA inner loops with simdgroup-MMA tensor-core execution.

problem.statement: Metal GEMM kernels written with scalar multiply-accumulate reach only single-digit percent of the MMA peak; a measured onyx-infer tile16 q4 kernel ran at ~2.1 TFLOPS vs MLX quantized_matmul at an estimated roofline on the same shape.

payload.technique: simdgroup MMA with single-round fp16 dequant
payload.what: Stage activation tiles as fp16 in threadgroup memory; unpack q4 nibbles, apply the fp32 group scale once, round the product to fp16, and feed fixed 8x8 half fragments to simdgroup_multiply_accumulate with an fp32 accumulator. One simdgroup (32 threads) per threadgroup owning a 32x32 output tile is a simple, correct starting topology.
payload.when: Quantized GEMM/MLP operators on M-series GPUs where the packing format must stay unchanged and numeric profile requires fp32 accumulation.
payload.how: 1. Declare simdgroup_matrix<half,8,8> fragment registers outside the k-loop. 2. Step k by 8; stage A as thread lane=row (8 iterations), dequant B nibbles per output column. 3. Load a/b fragments into registers once per step, then run a pure 4x4 MMA loop. 4. Accumulate in fp32 fragments, store through a threadgroup float tile. Never place simdgroup ops inside thread-conditional branches: they are collective over the simdgroup.
caveats: simdgroup_multiply_accumulate in metal4 toolchains takes 4 args (d, a, b, c), not 3
hoisting fragment loads into a conditional branch broke MMA/load pipelining and regressed 13.3ms -> 55ms
